Consult Summary:
34-year-old woman with 6-day history of dysuria, malodorous urine, intermittent midline lower-abdominal pain, and microscopic haematuria; no fever or flank pain. Clinical impression: uncomplicated lower urinary tract infection; oral antibiotics prescribed with hydration and safety-net advice.

History:
• Presenting complaint – “It hurts when I pee” for 6 days.  
• Symptoms – Dysuria, foul-smelling urine, intermittent mid-lower-abdominal pain (7/10, colicky), and spotting of blood in urine.  
• Progression – Ongoing for 6 days; pain comes and goes, not improving.  
• Associated / review of systems – No fever/rigors (no thermometer at home), no flank or loin pain, no difficulty initiating stream, able to void normal volumes, no vaginal discharge, normal bowel habit, no weight loss.  
• Exacerbating/relieving factors – None identified.  
• Triggers – Denies recent dehydration, strenuous exercise, or increased sexual activity.  
• First episode – Denies prior urinary infections.  

Past Medical History:
• Irritable bowel syndrome (IBS); no recent exacerbation, no complications noted.  
• Denies kidney disease or previous UTIs.  
• No past surgeries reported.

Medications:
• Mebeverine 200 mg orally three times daily (regular).  
Allergies:
• Clindamycin – reaction not specified (allergy documented).  

Social History:
• Lives with friends.  
• Occupation: Support worker.  
• Alcohol: ~1 glass wine/week (occasional).  
• Smoking: Never smoker.  
• Recreational drugs: Not mentioned.

Family History:
• Denies significant familial medical conditions.

Physical Examination:
(No in-person examination performed; no vitals reported.)

Investigations:
• None ordered; empiric treatment initiated.

Assessment & Plan:
Issue 1: Suspected acute uncomplicated cystitis  
  – Empiric diagnosis based on dysuria, malodorous urine, suprapubic pain, microscopic haematuria, no systemic features.  
  Plan:  
  • Prescribed 3-day course of antibiotics (drug/dose/route/frequency not documented) sent electronically to Knightsbridge pharmacy; patient to start ASAP.  
  • Hydration: Encourage 2.5–3 L water daily.  
  • Adjuncts: Consider cranberry juice; OTC urinary alkalinizing sachets (details to be added to notes).  
  • Monitoring: Purchase thermometer; check temperature periodically.  
  • Safety-net: Return/seek care if worsening pain, development of fever, flank pain, urinary retention, or persistent/recurrent symptoms.  

General plan items:  
• Follow-up only if symptoms persist or recur.  
• No routine post-treatment review required if fully recovered.

Quality checks (document_quality):
● Missing data expected in standard consult: vitals, objective abdominal/urinary exam, urine dip/urine culture, detailed antibiotic name/dose/route.  
● No internal transcript conflicts noted.  
● Transcript quality adequate; occasional minor audio gaps but did not obscure clinical content.
